items.title: Boot into the Live Environment
items.text:
• Insert the NCOS installation media (USB or ISO).
  • Boot from the installation media.
  • The live environment will load, and the installer will launch automatically.

items.title: Select Region, Timezone, and System Language
items.text:
• Choose your preferred region and timezone.
  • Select the system language for your installation.

items.title: Configure Keyboard Layout
items.text:
• Pick your keyboard layout from the available options.
  • Test the layout to ensure it's correct.

items.title: Partition the Drive
items.text:
Choose the target drive for installation then select one of the partitioning methods:

  1. Install alongside existing OS – Keeps current partitions and installs NCOS alongside.
  2. Replace a partition – Overwrites an existing partition with NCOS.
  3. Erase disk – Deletes all partitions and installs NCOS on a clean disk.
  4. Manual partitioning – Allows advanced users to create custom partitions.

btrfs by default

NCOS 2.0 installs use the btrfs filesystem with zstd compression and a full subvolume layout. This enables instant system snapshots you can boot into from the GRUB menu — see Backups & Snapshots after installing.

Dual-booting?

If you install NCOS alongside another OS, enable the multiboot GRUB menu after your first boot so you can pick between systems — see Dual Boot.

items.title: Create a User
items.text:
• Enter a username and password for your account.
  • Optionally, enable automatic login or require a password at startup.

items.title: Begin Installation
items.text:
• Review your settings.
  • Click Install to begin the process.
  • Wait for the installation to complete, then reboot into your new NCOS system.

items.title: Pre-Installation Guide
items.text: Before installing NCOS, follow these steps to prepare your system:

items.title: Download the NCOS ISO
items.text:
• Visit the NCOS official website for the download link.
  • Download the latest NCOS ISO file (currently NCOS 2.0).

items.title: Flash the ISO to a USB Drive
items.text:
You need to create a bootable USB drive using the NCOS ISO. Here are two recommended tools:

WindowsLinux
  • Download and install Rufus on your Windows PC.
  • Open Rufus.
  • Select your USB drive from the "Device" dropdown menu.
  • Click "Select" and choose the NCOS ISO file.
  • Ensure the "Partition scheme" is set to GPT.
  • Leave the file system settings as default (usually FAT32).
  • Click "Start" to begin creating the bootable USB.
  • Once complete, safely eject the USB drive.
  • Download and install Etcher on your system.
  • Open Etcher.
  • Click "Flash from file" and select the NCOS ISO file.
  • Insert your USB drive, and Etcher will automatically detect it.
  • Click "Flash" to begin writing the ISO to the USB drive.
  • Wait for the process to complete.
  • Safely remove the USB drive from your system.

items.title: Configure Your BIOS and Boot from USB
items.text:
To boot into the NCOS live environment, follow these steps:

  1. Access the BIOS/UEFI:

    • Restart your computer and enter the BIOS/UEFI settings. The key to access the BIOS varies by manufacturer (e.g., F2, F10, Del, or Esc). Consult your system's manual for details.

  2. Disable Secure Boot:

    • Locate the Secure Boot option in your BIOS settings.
    • Disable Secure Boot to allow booting from the NCOS USB.

  3. Set USB as Boot Priority:

    • Navigate to the Boot Menu in your BIOS.
    • Set the USB drive as the first boot device.

  4. Save and Exit:

    • Save your changes and exit the BIOS.

items.title: Step 4: Enter the Live Environment
items.text:
• Insert your bootable USB drive into the target machine.
  • Restart the system. It should boot directly into the NCOS live environment.
  • If it doesn't boot, ensure that the USB is set as the first boot device in the BIOS settings.

items.title: You're now ready to proceed with the Installation Process!
NCOS Assistant
items.text:
The NCOS Assistant is a built-in AI assistant that lives right in your panel and dock. It can answer questions about NCOS — shortcuts, how-tos, system tasks — using the built-in NCOS documentation, and it works as a general chat assistant too.

Fully offline by default

The Assistant runs entirely on your machine using Ollama with a compact local chat model and an embedding model for searching the NCOS docs. Nothing you type is sent to the cloud.

items.title: Setup
items.text:
Before first use, enable Ollama and pull the models the Assistant relies on:

sudo systemctl enable --now ollama
ollama pull embeddinggemma:300m
ollama pull llama3.2:1b

items.title: Where to Find It
items.text:
Add the applet to your panel:

COSMIC Settings → Desktop → Panel → Configure panel applets → Add "NCOS Assistant" — the chat-bubble icon appears in the panel.

items.title: What It Can Do
items.text:
• Answer NCOS questions — it has the NCOS documentation built in, so you can ask things like "how do I change the theme?" or "how do I take a snapshot?" and get an answer specific to your system.
  • General chat — quick questions, command syntax, explanations, all offline.
  • Stay private — models run locally; no account, no API key, no internet required.

Example

Ask: "How do I switch to the red theme?" — the Assistant will point you to the theme cycle shortcut (Super+Shift+]) described in Themes & Wallpapers.

items.title: Feeding It Your Wiki
items.text:
Drop .md (or .txt) files into docs/ — that folder is indexed by default. Add more folders in the applet's settings (gear icon). The index rebuilds automatically when files change (checked when the popup opens), or manually via Settings → Rebuild.

Info

The index is stored at ~/.local/share/ncos-assistant/index.json.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Settings live in the popup (gear icon) and persist via cosmic-config under ~/.config/cosmic/io.github.exothermic88.ncos-assistant/v1/:

  • Ollama server — local by default (localhost:11434); toggle "Use remote server" to point at another machine on your network.
  • Models — chat model (default llama3.2:1b) and embedding model (default embeddinggemma:300m). Changing the embedding model invalidates the index and triggers a rebuild.
  • Context chunks — how many document chunks are retrieved per question.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• The first response after boot can take a few seconds while the local model loads — after that it stays warm.
  • Because the models are small enough to run on modest hardware, keep questions focused for the best answers. For deep troubleshooting, the Arch Wiki remains your best friend.

items.title: Backups & Snapshots
items.text: NCOS 2.0 installs on btrfs by default, which makes system snapshots cheap and instant. Combined with Timeshift (preinstalled) and grub-btrfs, you can roll back a broken update by simply picking a snapshot from your boot menu.

items.title: Take Backups with Timeshift
items.text:
Timeshift snapshots your system so you can restore it if something breaks.

  1. Open Timeshift from the App Library (Super+A).
  2. On first run, choose the BTRFS snapshot type (recommended on NCOS 2.0 installs).
  3. Pick a schedule (e.g. daily or weekly) — or take manual snapshots with Create.

Tip

Take a manual snapshot before big changes — major updates, kernel upgrades, or experimenting with system configs: 

sudo timeshift --create --comments "before update"

items.title: Bootable Snapshots with auto-snapshot
items.text:
The new auto-snapshot command connects Timeshift to your GRUB boot menu: every snapshot you take shows up as a bootable entry.

Run it once:

auto-snapshot

This enables the grub-btrfs daemon, which watches for new Timeshift snapshots and adds them to the GRUB menu automatically.

btrfs only

auto-snapshot requires a btrfs root filesystem. Fresh NCOS 2.0 installs use btrfs by default; if you chose a different filesystem during manual partitioning, this feature isn't available.

items.title: Restoring After a Bad Update
items.text:
If an update leaves your system broken:

  1. Reboot and hold/press the boot menu key to show GRUB (if hidden — see Dual Boot for making the menu always visible).
  2. Open the snapshots submenu and boot into a snapshot from before the problem.
  3. Once booted, open Timeshift and click Restore on that snapshot to make the rollback permanent.

items.title: Dual Boot
items.text: By default NCOS boots instantly — the GRUB menu is hidden and the timeout is zero. If you dual-boot with Windows or another Linux, use multiboot-toggle to switch to a visible boot menu that detects your other operating systems.

items.title: Enable the Multiboot Menu
items.text:
sudo multiboot-toggle enable

This switches GRUB to the multiboot profile and regenerates the boot configuration with os-prober enabled — other installed operating systems (like Windows) are detected and added to the menu automatically. On your next reboot you'll see a GRUB menu listing every OS.

Tip

Installed another OS after enabling multiboot? Just run sudo multiboot-toggle enable again to re-scan and pick it up.

items.title: Return to Instant Boot
items.text:
sudo multiboot-toggle disable

This restores the hidden, zero-timeout menu for the fastest possible boot into NCOS.

Info

Even with the menu hidden, you can still reach GRUB by holding Shift (BIOS) or repeatedly pressing Esc (UEFI) during boot — useful for reaching the snapshot entries without enabling the full multiboot menu.

items.title: Welcome to the NCOS Wiki
items.text:
NCOS is a lightweight, rolling-release Linux distro built on Arch Linux with the COSMIC desktop. It's ready out of the box: tiling, themes, snapshots, and an offline AI assistant are already set up. This wiki covers installing NCOS and getting the most out of it.

What's new in NCOS 2.1.3

A Now Playing panel applet, the Tiling Assistant for choosing which apps float, Ollama on the ISO so the Assistant works right away, and a tuned grub-btrfs setup. See the release notes.

items.title: Get Started
items.text:
• Install NCOS

    Make a bootable USB and walk through the installer step by step.

  • Keyboard Shortcuts

    Launch apps, move windows, and switch workspaces from the keyboard.

  • How-To

    Quick answers to common everyday tasks.

  • NCOS Assistant

    Ask the offline AI assistant in your panel how to do things on NCOS.

    Switch between themes and pick wallpapers with a single shortcut.

items.title: Get Help & Contribute
items.text:
• New to NCOS? Start with the installation guide, then learn the keyboard shortcuts.
  • Found a bug or have an idea? Open an issue on the GitHub repository. Patches and documentation fixes are welcome too.
  • Need the ISO? Get the latest release from the NCOS website.

📘 Tip: Use the search bar at the top to quickly find topics of interest.

items.title: How-To Guides
items.text:
Quick, task-focused guides for common things you'll want to do on NCOS. Each section below covers one task start to finish.

Bigger topics have their own pages:

  • NCOS Assistant — the built-in offline AI assistant
  • Themes & Wallpapers — theme cycling, wallpaper picker, panorama wallpapers
  • Backups & Snapshots — Timeshift and bootable GRUB snapshots
  • Dual Boot — enabling the multiboot menu with multiboot-toggle

items.title: Mirror or Share Your Screen
items.text: NCOS gives you a couple of ways to share your display depending on what you're connecting to.

items.title: Option 1: Mirror to a Second Monitor (Wired/HDMI/DisplayPort)
items.text:
If you've plugged in a second monitor or TV and want it to show the exact same thing as your main display:

  1. Open Settings (Super+;).
  2. Go to Displays.
  3. Select the second display and enable mirroring (when mirroring is off, displays extend instead).
  4. Choose your preferred resolution/refresh rate, then click Apply.

Info

If the second display doesn't show up, check the physical cable connection first, then re-open Displays — it's usually detected automatically.

items.title: Option 2: Wireless Screen Casting (Miracast)
items.text:
To cast your screen to a wireless display or smart TV without any cables, NCOS ships GNOME Network Displays.

  1. Open the Network Displays app from the App Library (Super+A).
  2. Make sure the display you want to cast to is powered on and discoverable (most smart TVs need Miracast/Screen Mirroring mode enabled in their own settings).
  3. Select the display from the list and click Connect.

Warning

Wireless casting requires a Wi-Fi adapter that supports Wi-Fi Direct. Most modern laptop cards do, but some desktop USB adapters don't.

To stop mirroring, open Network Displays again and click Disconnect.

items.title: Share Files Between Devices
items.text:
NCOS 2.0 includes LocalSend — an open-source AirDrop alternative that works between Linux, Windows, macOS, Android, and iOS over your local network.

  1. Open LocalSend from the App Library (Super+A).
  2. Install LocalSend on the other device (localsend.org).
  3. Both devices appear automatically when on the same network — pick a file and send.

items.title: Flash a USB Drive
items.text:
Need to write an ISO to a USB stick (for example, to make an NCOS installer for a friend)? NCOS 2.0 ships Popsicle:

  1. Open Popsicle from the App Library (Super+A).
  2. Choose the ISO image, select the USB drive, and click Flash.

items.title: Add NCOS Repository
items.text:
Follow these steps to add the NCOS repository to your system and access NCOS-specific packages.

Preconfigured on NCOS 2.0 and later

Systems installed from an NCOS 2.0 or later ISO already have the [ncos] repository enabled — you can install any package below directly with sudo pacman -S. The setup steps further down are for older installs or other Arch-based systems.

items.title: First-Party Packages
items.text: Package What it is ncos-assistant The NCOS Assistant — offline local-AI panel applet ncos-package-update-applet Panel applet showing pending package updates ncos-weather-applet Panel weather applet ncos-now-playing-applet Panel applet showing the currently playing track, with album art (any MPRIS player) ncos-tiling-assistant Tiling Assistant — GUI for choosing which apps open floating instead of auto-tiled

items.title: Steps to Add the NCOS Repository
items.text:
1. Open pacman.conf file:

Use the following command to open the pacman.conf file in any text editor:

txt /etc/pacman.conf
2. Add NCOS repository configuration:

Append the following text to the end of the file:

[ncos]
SigLevel = Optional TrustAll
Server = https://raw.githubusercontent.com/exothermic88/ncos-repo/main/$arch
3. Synchronize NCOS repository:

Run the following command to add the NCOS repository to pacman (1):

  1. To learn more about pacman for package maintanance, refer to the arch wiki.

sudo pacman -Syy
4. Install NCOS-specific package:

Use the following command to install a NCOS package:

sudo pacman -S ncos-package_name

Example

sudo pacman -S ncos-assistant

items.title: Future Updates
items.text:
When future updates are released for ncos packages that you have already installed, they are installed along with your regular system update — just run:

sudo pacman -Syu

No other command is needed.

items.title: NCOS 2.1.3
items.text: New first-party apps for the panel and window tiling, the Assistant working out of the box, and a tuned snapshot setup.

items.title: New Features
items.text:
• Now Playing applet — new ncos-now-playing-applet shows the current track in the panel with album art and Artist – Title, for any MPRIS media player. Added to the panel by default.
  • Tiling Assistant — new ncos-tiling-assistant GUI for managing auto-tiling exceptions (apps that open floating). COSMIC Settings, Discord and Spotify float by default.
  • Ollama included — ollama now ships on the ISO, so the NCOS Assistant works out of the box.
  • grub-btrfs config — snapshot boot entries are titled by date and description, and Docker/container subvolumes are ignored. See Backups & Snapshots.
  • Accessibility zoom — preconfigured with mouse zoom shortcuts and 50% steps.
  • Refreshed installer slideshow — new artwork, updated text, and shortcut cards matching the current defaults (Super+B browser, Super+; settings).

items.title: Changes & Removals
items.text:
• Borderless panel by default.
  • broadcom-wl removed from the ISO.
  • ncos-theming no longer installed — theming files ship directly in /usr.
  • Config cleanup — removed leftover settings for applets NCOS doesn't ship.

items.title: NCOS 2.0
items.text: The biggest NCOS release yet — a built-in local AI assistant, btrfs installs with bootable snapshots, a full theme system, and a slimmer, faster ISO.

items.title: New Features
items.text:
• NCOS Assistant — a first-party COSMIC applet that puts a local AI assistant in your panel and dock. Runs fully offline via Ollama and can answer questions about NCOS using the built-in documentation. See the Assistant guide.
  • First-party applets — new ncos-package-update-applet and ncos-weather-applet ship preconfigured in the panel.
  • Theme system — three complete themes (Nord, Red, Purple) restyle COSMIC, kitty, and VS Code together. Cycle with Super+Shift+] / Super+Shift+[. See Themes & Wallpapers.
  • Wallpaper picker — Super+Shift+W opens a visual wallpaper grid, backed by the new awww wallpaper daemon with automatic panorama splitting for dual-monitor wallpapers.
  • btrfs by default — the installer now creates a btrfs filesystem with a full subvolume layout (@, @home, @root, @srv, @cache, @log, @tmp) and zstd compression.
  • Bootable snapshots — the new auto-snapshot command wires Timeshift snapshots into the GRUB menu via grub-btrfs. See Backups & Snapshots.
  • Dual-boot toggle — multiboot-toggle enable|disable switches GRUB between a hidden instant boot and a multiboot menu that detects other operating systems. See Dual Boot.
  • Redesigned installer — Calamares 2.0 branding with a new sidebar, navigation, and an all-new slideshow.

items.title: New Default Apps
items.text:
• COSMIC Store — graphical app installation.
  • COSMIC Monitor — system monitoring.
  • LocalSend — share files with nearby devices.
  • Popsicle — flash USB drives.
  • Android Messages — text from your desktop.
  • rofi — powers the new wallpaper picker.

items.title: Changes & Removals
items.text:
• Pamac removed — use pacman, yay, or COSMIC Store instead.
  • KDE Connect no longer preinstalled — install kdeconnect manually if you use it.
  • Legacy xf86-video drivers dropped — the modern modesetting driver is used.
  • Slimmer system — the full Qt6 group was trimmed to just what's needed, saving over a gigabyte of installed size.
  • Faster ISO — squashfs compression switched from xz to zstd for quicker boot and install.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Custom Brave Browser Extension: Added a custom extension for the Brave browser that allows users to effortlessly pull out a specific tab into a new window.
Instructions to Apply Brave Update

  1. Load the Extension

    • Open brave://extensions/.
    • Enable Developer Mode.
    • Click Load unpacked and select the BraveExtension folder in /.config/.

  2. Use the Shortcut

    • Press Ctrl+Shift+X (or your chosen shortcut) to detach the current tab into a new window.

items.title: Fixes
items.text:
• Discord Streaming Issue: Resolved an issue where Discord streaming failed to initialize properly.
Warning

Currently, for this fix to work you need to run xwaylandvideobridge before streaming due to current issues with the application on autostart. This will be fixed in future updates.

install/update the ncos-hotfix (1) package to enjoy these enhancements!

  1. How to Install ncos-hotfix

items.title: Themes & Wallpapers
items.text: NCOS ships with a coordinated theme system: switching a theme restyles COSMIC, the kitty terminal, and VS Code together, and swaps the wallpaper to match — all with a single keystroke.

items.title: Switching Themes
items.text:
Four complete themes are included: Nord (default), Red, Purple, and Green.

Action Shortcut Command Next theme Super+Shift+] theme-select.sh Previous theme Super+Shift+[ theme-select-previous.sh Toggle light/dark Super+Ctrl+] toggle_light_dark Pick a wallpaper Super+Shift+W wallpaper picker

Picking a wallpaper also switches themes: each wallpaper belongs to a theme, and selecting one from the picker switches your system to that wallpaper's theme — choose a wallpaper from the green folder and the Green theme is applied along with it.

When you cycle themes, your current COSMIC, kitty, and VS Code settings are saved back into the active theme before the next one is applied — so any tweaks you make to a theme stick with it.

Tip

Your active theme is remembered across reboots (it's stored in ~/.current_theme).

items.title: Picking a Wallpaper
items.text:
Press Super+Shift+W to open the wallpaper picker — a visual grid of all your wallpapers with thumbnails. Select one and it's applied instantly.

Wallpapers are organized per theme under ~/.config/wallpapers/, with one folder per theme: nord, red, purple, and green. Put your own images into the folder of the theme they belong to and they'll show up in the picker — the folder determines which theme a wallpaper is tied to, and picking it switches the system to that theme.

items.title: Multi-Monitor Panorama Wallpapers
items.text:
NCOS 2.0 uses the awww wallpaper daemon, which supports panorama splitting: wallpapers with dual in their filename are automatically split across your monitors, so one ultra-wide image spans both displays seamlessly.

Info

Name a wide wallpaper something like mountains-dual.png, place it in your theme's wallpaper folder, and select it with Super+Shift+W — NCOS handles the split for each monitor's position and resolution automatically.

items.title: Maintaining NCOS ensures a smooth and efficient system. Follow these Directions to keep your system up to date and running optimally.
Keeping the System Updated
items.text:
To update all packages, run: 

sudo pacman -Syu
To update AUR packages only, run: 
yay --aur
For a full system upgrade including AUR packages : 
yay

items.title: Removing Unused Packages
items.text:
Warning

Always double check the package list before deleting

To remove orphaned packages: 

sudo pacman -Rns $(pacman -Qdtq)

items.title: Clearing the Package Cache
items.text:
To free up disk space: 

sudo pacman -Sc  # Remove old package versions
sudo pacman -Scc # Remove all cached packages

items.title: Managing Services
items.text:
Check the status of a service: 

systemctl status <service-name>
Enable a service at startup: 
sudo systemctl enable <service-name>
Disable a service: 
sudo systemctl disable <service-name>
Restart a service: 
sudo systemctl restart <service-name>

items.title: Checking System Logs
items.text:
View logs for troubleshooting: 

journalctl -xe
View logs for a specific service: 
journalctl -u <service-name> --no-pager

items.title: Monitoring System Resources
items.text:
To check system resource usage: 

htop
To check disk usage: 
df -h
